findings.description: This categorical wording gives a misleading next-word diagnostic. An article can be followed by an adjective before the noun: el nuevo libro.
findings.suggestion: Explain that the article introduces a noun phrase and that an adjective may intervene, as lesson step s6 already explains.

findings.location: task.prompt[0].text: "про себе й колегу, якого він ще не бачив"; task.errors[id=e1]: "Soy estudiante y es profesor." marked incorrect; feedbackUk: "Без él незрозуміло, хто викладач".
findings.description: Not having seen the colleague does not establish whether he has already been introduced in the exchange. If he is a salient antecedent, the tacit subject of es may be recoverable; if he has not been introduced, reference is insufficiently established. The packet does not supply the discourse needed to justify categorical rejection.
findings.suggestion: Supply the preceding exchange and specify whether the colleague has already been introduced. Review the omitted-subject answer against that discourse; alternatively, explicitly require an overt pronoun for contrast.

items.reviewerAnswer: Yo soy estudiante y él es profesor. Also: Soy estudiante y él es profesor. Whether Soy estudiante y es profesor is acceptable depends on the preceding discourse.
items.notes: The distinction between an unseen colleague and an unmentioned colleague is inferred from the prompt wording; the latter condition is not stated.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 33, tacit subjects and contextual recoverability (from memory).
Packet, task:A1-03-L1-T45, task.prompt[0]: the colleague has not been seen; no preceding exchange is supplied.
